input.quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
input.rationale: Kubient gives affirmative warranties that run for the whole Term (no 12-month/90-day cut-off), including performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from errors materially affecting utility (p0038), no malicious code (p0036) and compliance with Laws (p0041), and the paragraph 13 disclaimer expressly carves out "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement", so it does not swallow the express warranty. Duration and scope therefore exceed the preferred position. However, the Agreement contains no warranty remedy at all — there is no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund right anywhere (only the general 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b)), and "refund" appears nowhere in the document. Remedy is a material term of both the preferred and fallback positions, so we added the standard remedy sentence at Kubient's option after paragraph 9(b), preserving our other rights. We did not touch the period or disclaimer, which are already compliant; the absence of express "professional and workmanlike" wording is covered by the industry-standards warranty and is not flagged.

ops.text: For any breach of the warranties in this paragraph 9(b), Customer's remedy is, at Kubient's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Service, repair or replacement of the non-conforming deliverable, or a refund of the fees paid or payable for the non-conforming Service or deliverable, in each case without limiting Customer's other rights and remedies under this Agreement or at Law.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Kubient's performance warranties have no stated remedy, so we added the standard repair/re-perform-or-refund remedy for non-conforming Services or deliverables, at Kubient's option and without waiving our other rights. This matches our playbook position that a warranty must be backed by a real remedy.
proposal.summary: Add an express warranty remedy (re-performance, repair/replacement or refund) for breach of Kubient's warranties.
